pr_title: lib: refactor lazy loading of undici for fetch method
pr_body:
Object.defineProperty is updated to lazily load the undici dependency for the fetch method. This change allows for simpler and more reliable mocking of the fetch method for testing purposes, resolving issues encountered with premature method invocation during testing.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/52015

issue_context.title: breaking change in 21.7.0 when mocking fetch
comments: It seems to me that it’s t.mock that should be fixed,  other wise it would not work with user land objects that has a similar descriptor.

I think the bug comes from the `fetch` method, because I have the same problem with https://github.com/sinonjs/sinon/issues/2590 (which doesn't use `mock`).

The descriptor of property `fetch` is different before and after using it.

```JavaScript
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, "fetch"));
fetch;
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, "fetch"));
```

- Node.js v21.7.0:

  ```JavaScript
  {
    get: [Function: get],
    set: [Function: set],
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true
  }
  {
    value: [Function: fetch],
    writable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true
  }
  ```

- Node.js v21.6.2:

  ```JavaScript
  {
    value: [Function: fetch],
    writable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true
  }
  {
    value: [Function: fetch],
    writable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true
  }
  ```

- Chromium 122:

  ```JavaScript
  {
    writable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true,
    value: f fetch()
  }
  {
    writable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    configurable: true,
    value: f fetch()
  }
  ```
@regseb That was done in #51598 for performance reasons. Your best course of actions is to trigger all the getters before your tests start.
@regseb That was done in #51598 for performance reasons. Your best course of actions is to trigger all the getters before your tests start.

At end of the day, it seems to be a design issue with the mocking libraries, as their API forces users to know and differentiate between getters and values even though users may only care about hijacking or recording the access, but don’t care about whether the access is done via a getter or not. For example with Sinon I think you would then need to use a spy with .get(), and this applies to user objects too https://github.com/sinonjs/sinon/issues/1545 That said for properties that are themselves methods, like in the case of fetch, doing the lazy loading inside the value method seems to be a good compromise if it helps users work around this issue with the mocking libraries. I am not sure about FormData and friends because as constructors wrapping them complicates instanceof, but they may be less necessary to mock anyway.
In any case, isn't it still considered a breaking change and should be in a major node version change?

There's the same problem with Node v20.12.0:

- https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/bd2a3c10aeff38281992b8437a9f6e1830ba9d6f _lib: define FormData and fetch etc. in the built-in snapshot_
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52212
Same problem reproduced with Node v20.12.1
The bug is also in v22.0.0: https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/ce5688782e277459681538ce1658e8b0ee4189af
Is there a reason why this issue is marked as closed? The issue still persists into v22.0.0 and wasn't fixed by #52275 . Has the discussion moved somewhere else?
@yeoffrey https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52275 includes a test demonstrating this was indeed fixed. can you please provide a reproduction code that fails on v22?
https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52275 is not yet in v22. It should be part of the next release.

> @yeoffrey #52275 includes a test demonstrating this was indeed fixed. can you please provide a reproduction code that fails on v22?

Sorry about that. @targos's answer clears it up for me, cheers 👍

review_comments: I think it's to specify that the `init` argument is optional.
right, but you're defaulting it to undefined -.which would be the case if it wasn't defined, it's redundant

Same comment for https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/deps/undici/undici.js#L12497

It makes no sense to default an argument value to undefined ever

It affects the `.length` of the function, which is observable. Parameters with default values don't count towards the length. And since the correct length is 1, not 2, this is the only way to do that without either explicitly setting the length attribute or referencing `arguments`.
